neighbours.label: ' play' / ' call' / ' kick' / ' take' opening a casual fixed phrase ('play it safe', 'call it a day', 'play along', 'kick back', 'take it easy'). The same verbs used literally (play the violin, call my mother, take the books) and the noun 'play' stay weak.
fire: With the storm coming in, the captain chose to play it safe and stay in port.
By midnight the search team was ready to call it a night.
Nobody on the committee wanted to play hardball with the landlord.
After the exams the students just wanted to kick back for a week.
The doctor told him to take it easy for a few days after the operation.
We have no fixed plan for Saturday, so let's play it by ear.
After thirty years in the trade, the old carpenter decided to call it quits.
The witness refused to play along with the lawyer's little game.
quiet: With the storm coming in, the captain chose to stay in port and wait.
By midnight the search team was ready to call the families with news.
Nobody on the committee wanted to see the new play at the town hall.
After the exams the students wanted to kick a ball around the yard.
The doctor told him to take the tablets for a few days after the operation.
My sister can play the cello and the flute quite well.
After thirty years in the trade, the old carpenter decided to sell his tools.
The witness will take the stand again on Monday morning.
